title: Extension of scalars of a vector space along a field extension
statement: Let $K\subset L$ be fields ($L$ a field extension of $K$) and $V$ a $K$-vector space. The *extension of scalars* of $V$ to $L$ is the tensor product $V\otimes_KL$, an $L$-vector space with $\lambda\cdot(v\otimes\mu)=v\otimes\lambda\mu$. A $K$-linear map $f:V\to W$ induces the $L$-linear map $f\otimes_KL:V\otimes_KL\to W\otimes_KL$, $v\otimes\mu\mapsto f(v)\otimes\mu$, and $V\mapsto V\otimes_KL$ is a functor from $K$-vector spaces to $L$-vector spaces. If $(v_j)_{j\in J}$ is a $K$-basis of $V$ then $(v_j\otimes1)_{j\in J}$ is an $L$-basis of $V\otimes_KL$; in particular $V\otimes_KL$ is finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] over $L$ when $V$ is finite-dimensional over $K$, of the same dimension. For a tower $K\subset L\subset M$ of fields there is a canonical $M$-linear isomorphism $(V\otimes_KL)\otimes_LM\cong V\otimes_KM$, $(v\otimes\lambda)\otimes\mu\mapsto v\otimes\lambda\mu$, natural in $V$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Algebra, Section 'Tensor products' (Tag 00CV) and Lemma 00D0 (associativity, giving (V⊗_K L)⊗_L M ≅ V⊗_K(L⊗_L M) = V⊗_K M); Section 'Base change' (Tag 05G3), Definition 05G4 and Lemma 05G5 (base change of a finite module is finite); the basis statement is elementary (tensor product commutes with direct sums)
